analyst_view.overall: Early view: Real Madrid are 2nd with a perfect 12 points and have won eight in a row under Jose Mourinho, most recently 3-0 at Valencia; Vinicius Junior's suspension is a LaLiga one and does not apply in Europe, though Mourinho says he is not sure of a start. PSV (24th, 4 points) lost 2-1 at home to Club Brugge on matchday 4 and sit on the edge of the play-off places.

goals.text: The numbers say 4.6 goals and I lean lower. Madrid under Mourinho win with control: 3-0 at Valencia and 3-0 at Racing Santander in their last two league games. They did concede twice in Athens, but a home win by two or three goals looks more likely than a five-goal game.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners and I stay with it. Madrid will dominate at the Bernabeu, but they score plenty from open play through Jude Bellingham, Kylian Mbappe and Arda Guler. Nothing I found moves the figure.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.1 cards and I lean slightly lower. Madrid's win in Athens had only two bookings before AEK's late red card, and PSV's home defeat by Brugge had three, all for Brugge. One-sided games at the Bernabeu tend not to be card-heavy.

shots.text: The numbers say 31 shots. Madrid's attack is in form, with Bellingham passing 50 goals for the club and Federico Valverde scoring late in Athens, so a high volume is likely. PSV scored at home against Brugge and should add some shots on the break.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 12.6 shots on target, which is very high. Mourinho's sides tend to slow the game once ahead, and that dampens the second-half total. I lean slightly lower but still expect a busy night for PSV's goalkeeper.
